# Almost Lore

> Original longform on public-record historical near-misses and weird history.

## Stories

- [Poyais: the country that existed on paper](https://almostlore.com/stories/poyais-invented-country): Gregor MacGregor sold land, banknotes, and government posts in a country that did not exist. Then the settlers arrived.
- [The Darien scheme: Scotland’s ruinous shortcut](https://almostlore.com/stories/darien-scheme): Five ships sailed to build a Scottish trading colony in 1698. When the next expedition arrived, the settlement had already been abandoned.
- [Two flags at Fashoda](https://almostlore.com/stories/fashoda-incident-1898): A French column reached a ruined fort on the White Nile. An Anglo-Egyptian flotilla followed. In 1898, two imperial claims met at Fashoda.
- [The four men taken off the Trent](https://almostlore.com/stories/trent-affair): A Union captain seized four men from a British mail ship in 1861. Britain demanded their return. The Civil War nearly acquired another front.
- [The Pig War: one shot, thirteen years of waiting](https://almostlore.com/stories/pig-war-san-juan): A pig wandered into an American settler’s garden in 1859. His shot brought troops to San Juan Island, where the border remained unsettled until 1872.
- [The Caroline affair: a burning ship, an unsteady peace](https://almostlore.com/stories/caroline-affair): A British raid burned an American steamer on the Niagara in 1837. One man died. Years later, a murder trial threatened the peace again.
- [Dogger Bank: the night the navy fired at fishermen](https://almostlore.com/stories/dogger-bank-1904): A Russian squadron mistook Hull trawlers for a threat in 1904. Two fishermen died. Britain and Russia then had to prevent a second disaster.
- [The Venezuela crisis that threatened a wider war](https://almostlore.com/stories/venezuelan-crisis-1895): In 1895, an argument over British Guiana’s boundary brought a threat from Washington. A treaty eased the crisis. Its map did not settle the dispute.
- [The Aroostook War: a border without a battle](https://almostlore.com/stories/aroostook-war): Maine sent an armed posse into disputed forest in 1839. Arrests and military preparations followed. The Aroostook War ended at a negotiating table.
- [The last winter of Vitus Bering](https://almostlore.com/stories/bering-island-winter): His expedition reached the American coast. The voyage home ended in a wreck, a winter camp, and a boat the survivors had to build themselves.
